name: Rice Water Weevil
description: A semiaquatic weevil whose larvae feed on rice roots, causing reduced plant vigor, stunting, and yield loss. Adult weevils feed on leaves but the primary damage is from larval root feeding.
symptoms: Adult leaf feeding scars as longitudinal lines on leaves
Larvae feeding on roots causing root pruning
Stunted plant growth and reduced tillering
Plants appearing nutrient-stressed even with adequate fertilizer
Reduced panicle number and grain yield
Plants easily uprooted due to reduced root system
lifecycle: Egg (laid in leaf sheath below water)
treatments: Apply carbofuran granules early in the season at flooding
Use neem cake as soil amendment before planting
Drain fields for 3-5 days to reduce larval survival
prevention: Delay flooding for 2-3 weeks after planting to reduce weevil attraction
Practice crop rotation with dryland crops
Maintain field sanitation to reduce overwintering sites
Plant early to avoid peak weevil activity
